title: Find Palindrome With Fixed Length
description:
Given an integer array queries and a positive integer intLength, return an array answer where answer[i] is either the queries[i]th smallest positive palindrome of length intLength or -1 if no such palindrome exists.
A palindrome is a number that reads the same backwards and forwards. Palindromes cannot have leading zeros.

examples.text:
Input: queries = [1,2,3,4,5,90], intLength = 3
Output: [101,111,121,131,141,999]
Explanation:
The first few palindromes of length 3 are:
101, 111, 121, 131, 141, 151, 161, 171, 181, 191, 202, ...
The 90th palindrome of length 3 is 999.

Input: queries = [2,4,6], intLength = 4
Output: [1111,1331,1551]
Explanation:
The first six palindromes of length 4 are:
1001, 1111, 1221, 1331, 1441, and 1551.

hints: For any value of queries[i] and intLength, how can you check if there exists at least queries[i] palindromes of length intLength?
Since a palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards, consider how you can efficiently find the first half (ceil(intLength/2) digits) of the palindrome.
